extracted.intended_audience: applicants, licensees, potential parties, attorneys, NRC staff, presiding officers, and others participating in Nuclear Regulatory Commission adjudications and rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: The regulatory rules (10 CFR Part 2) that govern NRC proceedings—licensing, enforcement, hearings, petitions, filings, discovery, presiding officer authority, special procedures for classified material, and schedules—specifying procedural requirements and standards participants must meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope (§ 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part governs the conduct of all proceedings ... for (a) granting, suspending, revoking, amending, or taking other action with respect to any license, construction permit, or application to transfer a license; (b) issuing orders and demands for information to persons subject to the Commission's jurisdiction; (c) imposing civil penalties under Section 234 of the Act; (d) rulemaking under the Act and the Administrative Procedure Act; and (e) standard design approvals under part 52 or 53 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the range of proceedings covered by Part 2 and cites statutory authorities; sets the universe of actions subject to these procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subparts: special v. general rules (§ 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subpart other than subpart C sets forth special rules applicable to the type of proceeding described in the first section of that subpart. Subpart C sets forth general rules applicable to all types of proceedings except rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a proceeding has special rules in its subpart, those special rules govern; read subpart C together with the specific subpart for a proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of conflict (§ 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) In any conflict between a general rule in subpart C and a special rule in another subpart or other part of this chapter applicable to a particular type of proceeding, the special rule governs. (b) Unless otherwise specifically referenced, the procedures in this part do not apply to hearings in specified other CFR parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there's a conflict, apply the specific/special provision rather than the general one; lists exemptions where Part 2 procedures do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (§ 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key terms used in this part are defined (e.g., ACRS, Act, Adjudication, Administrative Law Judge, Commission, Commission adjudicatory employee, Contested proceeding, Electronic Hearing Docket, E-Filing System, Ex parte communication, Facility, Participant, Presiding officer, Safeguards Information, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions control interpretation of procedural obligations (e.g., who is a participant, what counts as ex parte communication, what is an Electronic Hearing Docket).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection requirements: OMB approval (§ 2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part contains no information collection requirements and therefore is not subject to requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that Part 2 itself does not impose Paperwork Reduction Act burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for issuance, amendment, transfer, or renewal of a license; standard design approval (Subpart A / § 2.100)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart prescribes the procedure for issuance of a license; amendment of a license at the request of the licensee; transfer and renewal of a license; and issuance of a standard design approval under subpart E of part 52 or subpart H of part 53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural baseline for applications relating to licensing and standard design approvals; see § 2.101 and related sections for filing and docketing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of application; tendered applications and docketing (§ 2.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be filed with the appropriate Director. A prospective applicant may confer informally with NRC staff. Applications will be assigned docket numbers. To determine completeness/acceptability, an application will initially be treated as a tendered application and generally a determination on acceptability for docketing will be made within 30 days (or 60 days in selected cases). A copy of the tendered application will be available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acceptable for docketing the applicant will be asked to: submit additional copies as required, serve copies and notices on chief executives of affected municipalities/counties, and provide brief description and docket number; timing (30/60 days) and public availability are mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing / issuance timing (§ 2.104 / § 2.101 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission directs that notice of hearing be issued as soon as practicable after tendering, notice of hearing will be issued consistent with determinations of acceptability for docketing and technical adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may proceed to issue hearing notice based on technical adequacy as well as completeness; filing/docketing procedures interact with hearing notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination (§ 2.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition of sex discrimination (section heading and placement indicate mandatory nondiscrimination obligations in the context of licensing and proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms nondiscrimination obligations apply in proceedings covered by Part 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart B enforcement procedures: notice of violation, orders, demands, civil penalties, requests (§ 2.200–2.206)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart B prescribes procedures for imposing requirements by order, modification/suspension/revocation of license, and imposing civil penalties: includes notice of violation, orders, demand for information, civil penalties under Section 234, and requests for action under the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies administrative enforcement mechanisms and procedural safeguards for enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for documents; signatures; acceptance for filing (§ 2.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed must meet formal requirements (formatting, signatures) and will be accepted for filing only when in compliance with applicable provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents that fail formal requirements may be rejected; see E-Filing guidance for electronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and service of documents; methods; proof (§ 2.305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of documents must follow specified methods and proof of service is required. The E‑Filing System and Electronic Hearing Docket are defined and used where an electronic hearing docket has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed electronic systems where available; provide proof of service; electronic acknowledgments confirm receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time (§ 2.306)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribes how to compute time limits for filings and other deadlines under Part 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines must be computed per the rules in §2.306 (e.g., excluding weekends/holidays where appropriate); extensions/reductions governed by §2.307.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and reduction of time limits; delegated authority (§ 2.307)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for extending or reducing time limits, and delegating authority to order procedures for access to certain sensitive unclassified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer or delegated authority may adjust time limits and order special procedures for sensitive information access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of hearing requests / petitions for leave to intervene (§ 2.308)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies how the Secretary treats requests for hearings and petitions to intervene (processing, timeliness, docketing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural processing steps and timing requirements for hearing/intervention requests are defined; see §2.309 for substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing requests, petitions to intervene, standing, and contentions (§ 2.309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets requirements for hearing requests and petitions to intervene, including requirements for standing and contentions. Contentions must include a specific statement of issue, the basis for the contention, the relief sought, and a concise statement of the facts or expert opinions supporting the contention with references. Petitioners must demonstrate standing and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a central gating rule: contentions must be specific, supported, and material to the proceeding; failure to satisfy §2.309 requirements is grounds for denial of intervention or exclusion of contentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of hearing procedures (§ 2.310)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission selects the hearing procedure (e.g., formal adjudication, hybrid, simplified, or legislative) appropriate to the matter and may direct use of certain subparts or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of procedure has implications for discovery, evidence, schedule, and participant rights; Commission discretion governs selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory review (§ 2.311)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for interlocutory review of rulings on requests for hearings/petitions to intervene, selection of hearing procedures, and requests for access to sensitive unclassified information and safeguards information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mechanism and scope for expedited review of certain interlocutory decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation, disqualification, substitution of presiding officer (§ 2.313)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for who may be designated as presiding officer, grounds and procedures for disqualification, and substitution when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures impartial adjudicators and provides procedures for recusal or substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance and practice before the Commission (§ 2.314)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies who may appear and practice before the Commission in adjudicatory proceedings and under what conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls admission to practice and representation of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation by persons not parties (§ 2.315)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows certain persons (e.g., interested State/local governmental bodies, federally-recognized Indian Tribes) to participate under defined conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines participant categories and their rights for participation distinct from full party status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of parties and proceedings (§ 2.316–2.317)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits consolidation of parties and/or proceedings when appropriate and provides standards for separate hearings or consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer may consolidate for efficiency or order separate hearings when issues differ materially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of the presiding officer (§ 2.319)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer has authority to take actions necessary to conduct the hearing (issue orders, set schedules, rule on motions, regulate discovery and evidence, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad managerial authority to ensure fair and expeditious proceedings; actions are subject to Commission review as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof (§ 2.325)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies who bears the burden of proof in proceedings (e.g., applicant or other party seeking relief) and related allocation matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes which party must prove facts or legal entitlement to relief in different types of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: General discovery and required disclosures (§ 2.336 and Subpart G / L nuances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the scope and methods of discovery, including required disclosures, production of documents, depositions, admissions, discovery against NRC staff, and limits (e.g., in Subpart L simplified hearings discovery may be prohibited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery procedures vary by subpart; some proceedings have comprehensive discovery rules (Subpart G), others limit or prohibit discovery (Subpart L). Mandatory disclosures may accelerate evidence exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence at a hearing (§ 2.337 / § 2.711 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing admissibility, form, and weighting of evidence, including treatment of restricted/classified evidence under Subpart I and evidentiary procedures (e.g., proposed findings and conclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer controls admissibility; classified/restricted evidence requires special procedures and may be subject to weight limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and alternative dispute resolution (§ 2.338)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits settlement of issues and use of alternative dispute resolution where appropriate, with procedures to implement settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages resolution of issues outside of full adjudication where possible; settlements must be entered on the record and meet procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision; effect and timing (§ 2.340 / § 2.713)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer issues initial decisions following close of record; rules govern immediate effectiveness of initial decisions in certain contested proceedings and issuance of authorizations, permits, and licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timing and effect of initial decisions and when they become effective pending Commission review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of presiding officer decisions and stays (§ 2.341–2.342)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides procedures for Commission review of presiding officer rulings and motions for stays of decisions, including grounds and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may seek Commission review; stays require demonstration of appropriate grounds and follow specified timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument and hearings to be public (§ 2.328, § 2.331, § 2.343)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings are to be public; provisions allow for oral argument before presiding officer and the Commission, subject to rules for public access and possible restrictions for sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access is the default; exceptions exist for protected information (e.g., Restricted Data, Safeguards Information) and certain closed sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for reconsideration and petitions for Commission review (§ 2.345, § 2.341)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets standards and procedures for filing petitions for reconsideration and requests for Commission review of presiding officer decisions and initial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness, content, and effect of petitions are governed by the referenced sections; petitions may trigger Commission action or stay considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications and separation of functions (§ 2.347–2.348)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines ex parte communications (oral or written communications not on the public record without reasonable prior notice to all parties) and imposes rules to prevent improper communications and separate investigative/decisional functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict restrictions on ex parte contacts and organizational separation apply to preserve fairness; special rules apply in legislative hearings and when classified information is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for Restricted Data / National Security Information (Subpart I: §§ 2.900–2.913)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposes special procedures to safeguard and prevent disclosure of Restricted Data or national security information: classification assistance, access, security clearances, notices of intent to introduce classified information, admissibility/weight of classified evidence, and review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must follow notice, clearance, and handling procedures; classified evidence may be rearranged or hearings suspended to protect national security; Unclassified statements may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart L simplified hearing procedures (§§ 2.1200–2.1213)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes streamlined procedures for certain adjudications, including prohibition on discovery (in some contexts), special processes and schedules for oral or written hearings, and rules for initial decisions, petitions for review, and stays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplified hearings shorten timelines and limit discovery; parties must follow specific schedules and submission formats under Subpart L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart M procedures for license transfer applications (§§ 2.1300–2.1331)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets procedures for public notice of receipt, availability of documents, written comments, oral hearings, presentation of testimony, conditions, presiding officer authority, schedules for submission, and Commission action on license transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes options for hearings consisting of written comments or oral hearings; provides for stay applications and Commission review of transfer-related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart N expedited proceedings with oral hearings (§§ 2.1400–2.1407)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides expedited procedures and limits for certain proceedings where the Commission elects oral hearing on accelerated schedule, with rules for prehearing conference, hearing, initial decisions, and appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for matters requiring faster resolution; parties should expect compressed timelines and constrained discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative hearings procedures (§§ 2.1500–2.1509)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for legislative hearings: Commission decision to hold, authority of presiding officer, requests to participate, role of NRC staff, written statements and submission of information, oral hearing rules, recommendation of presiding officer, and ex parte/separation of functions rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative hearings differ from adjudicatory hearings in scope and effect; presiding officer prepares certification and record for Commission consideration on identified issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B: Model Milestones for scheduling (Subpart G, L, M, N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model milestone schedules provide guideline timelines for major events in various types of proceedings (e.g., enforcement actions under Subpart G: answer within 20 days, presiding officer order within 100 days, discovery complete within 145 days, written testimony filed within 275 days, initial decision within 90 days after hearing close). Subpart L, M, and N have their own model milestone timelines tailored to the proceeding type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milestones are guidance for presiding officers to use as a starting point; presiding officers should modify them based on case complexity, admitted contentions, and NRC staff schedules. They reflect assumptions (e.g., issues involve factual disputes and regulatory compliance) and electronic filing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix D: Detailed schedule for high-level waste geologic repository proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a day-by-day schedule (Day 0, 30, 55, 62, 70, 100, etc.) mapping regulatory actions and filing deadlines for construction authorization proceedings for a high-level waste geologic repository (e.g., Federal Register Notice of Hearing at Day 0; petitions to intervene with contentions by Day 30; discovery complete by Day 608; evidentiary hearing begins Day 720; initial decision Day 955; Commission decision Day 1125).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a prescriptive timetable for a complex, specific proceeding type and illustrates how the model milestones and Part 2 timing rules interrelate; presiding officer may adjust per §2.332/2.334 but Appendix D represents a detailed planning benchmark.
